title: P37 / P34 x P32 topology: layer-wise instead of head-wise hybrid, ALiBi on all 8 heads of blocks 0, 2, 4 (115's slopes 1/4..1/256, each on two heads) and NoPE on all 8 heads of blocks 1, 3, 5, same slope multiset as 115-fable (4.80M params)
description: Idea ID: P37 (different positional scales at different depths) in its P34 x P32 hybrid form. 115-fable won with 4 ALiBi + 4 NoPE heads in every block; this keeps exactly the same 48 (block, head) slope slots (each of 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 six times, slope 0 twenty-four times) but arranges them by layer, alternating all-ALiBi and all-NoPE blocks as in Llama 4 / SmolLM3 / Command A's interleaved local and position-free layers, so a NoPE layer can spend all 8 heads on content lookup of cited lines at unseen lengths and an ALiBi layer can spend all 8 on local Lean syntax.
hypothesis: 115's gain over all-ALiBi 113 (+25.7, round-1 targets up) came from position-free heads that can find a cited premise by content at distances never seen in cap-6 pretraining. In the head-wise split each block has only 4 such heads, and every NoPE head output is mixed with local-head outputs in the same proj before the next block. A proof line cites up to 2-3 premises (and-intro, modus ponens) whose names must be matched; a dedicated all-NoPE layer has 8 content heads at once, and the following ALiBi layer can then do local syntax on the retrieved content with 8 distance resolutions. Interleaving local and position-free layers is what production long-context models (Llama 4 iRoPE, SmolLM3, Command A) chose for length extrapolation. If right: pretraining is statistically unchanged (4,150-4,300 steps; final val loss 0.078-0.085; held-out greedy ~0.98), round-1 targets solved at or above 115's 718/756/691, eval ge10+ at or above 115, and a metric above 631.33. If wrong, the likely reason is that NoPE heads need local ALiBi context in the same block (e.g. to form 'which name does this position cite' queries) so splitting them by layer loses that pairing; 058-claude's single NoPE layer under RoPE (-30, token format) is weak evidence for that. Mechanism checks: (a) round-1 targets solved and parse failures vs 115; (b) r1->r4 gain vs 115; (c) eval by_bin at 10-12 lines vs 115; (d) steps vs 115's 4204/4218/4263.
expected_delta: -45 to +35 dev solves >= 7 vs 115-fable's 631.33 (central -5); round-1 targets solved 650-780; pretraining steps 4,150-4,300, final val loss 0.078-0.085; totals 1,500-1,900 s under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (LayerNorm on each branch output as well as its input) and hybrid positional LAYERS: CHANGED from 115's per-head split to a per-block split, even blocks all-ALiBi and odd blocks all-NoPE (P37 / P34 x P32 topology)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope by layer (CHANGED from 115's 4+4 heads in every block): no rotation of q/k in any block; blocks 0, 2, 4 add -slope_h * (query position - key position) on all 8 heads via the SDPA attn_mask with slopes (1/4, 1/4, 1/16, 1/16, 1/64, 1/64, 1/256, 1/256), i.e. 115's 4-head standard set each on two heads; blocks 1, 3, 5 have slope 0 on all 8 heads (NoPE: bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys). Across the 48 (block, head) slots the multiset of slopes is identical to 115's: each of 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 on 6 slots and 0 on 24
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 115-fable: the slope table only. ALIBI_SLOPES/N_ALIBI replaced by BLOCK_SLOPES = (ALiBi row, NoPE row); ALiBiGPT's slopes buffer is (2, 1, H, 1, 1), the bias is built once per forward as (2, B or 1, H, T, S) and block i uses bias[i % 2]. PeriLNBlock, key positions in caches[0], mask handling, width, heads, depth, GELU, untied embedding/readout, ln_f, init, optimizer and schedule are byte-identical to 115. Same parameters and matmul FLOPs; one extra (T, S) bias slab per forward
arch.n_params_detail: identical to 115-fable, 113-fable and 107-claude: 4,800,000 (vocab 107); slopes buffer is not a parameter
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from this pretrain.py (its BLOCK_SLOPES), replace blocks with PeriLNBlock as in pretrain.py, then load state (same keys as 107/113/115). Loading these weights into 115's model (per-head table) gives a different function. The live harness uses the returned model object through RL and eval
arch.kv_cache: verified on CPU with fork 51604b3 (/private/tmp/fork51604b3): left-padded 3-prompt batch, prefill with pos/mask exactly as sample.generate_ids then 13 teacher-forced cached steps vs an unpadded full forward per row, max abs logit diff 8.9e-7; n_params 4,800,000

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: CHANGED: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: CHANGED: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, CHANGED: + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1
